# The data model

Generated from `src/domain/types.ts` (every record, field and the comment written beside it) and the migrations in `supabase/migrations`. The goals domain. Everything the screens show is derived from these records by the pure functions in plan.ts, status.ts and checkin.ts.

Every screen, export and AI tool derives what it shows from these records with the pure rules in `src/domain` (see [the rules](rules/README.md)). Ids are strings. Dates are ISO 8601: a day is `yyyy-mm-dd`, a moment a full UTC timestamp. Weeks are counted from a cycle’s start: week 0 is the first seven days.

## Keys, uniqueness and scope

The logical model: what identifies each record, what must be unique, and what each points to, as rules a rebuild holds in its own schema. Build from this, not from [schema.sql](schema.sql), which is Faro’s Postgres dump for reading. The limits on single fields (a title of at least 3 characters, a review every 1 to 13 weeks) are on their rules’ pages, under “Limits the records hold”.

- **Every record belongs to one workspace**, and a workspace is the unit of access ([R1](../requirements/internal/r1-sign-in-and-access.md)). Store the workspace on every row, and make it part of every key and every reference, so a reference to another workspace’s record can’t be stored. (Faro’s tables carry `workspace_id` but no foreign key to the workspace, and their references don’t include it.)
- **Ids are unique within their workspace.** Faro’s are global text ids made in the browser (`newId`); a rebuild’s server makes them, of whatever kind its platform uses.
- **References stay inside the workspace.** A goal’s owner, its team and the goal it feeds are all in its workspace.
- **Removing is marking.** A record with `removedAt` is kept for 30 days for undo and history (REMOVE-ANYTHING); uniqueness counts only records not removed, except a goal’s key, which is never given again.
- **Versions.** Goals and reviews carry a `version`; a save names the version it was based on and is refused if it has moved (NO-LOST-UPDATES). A refused save runs its action again on the latest, with the same input, and saves that, unless the input is a whole record as last seen or the person confirmed it against what they were shown (AX6). Other records are last write wins today: a rebuild extends versions to them and says how a clash is shown.

| Record | Key | Unique | Points to | Also |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Person | `id` | `email` within the workspace, when it has one, among people not removed; kept lower case | `teamId` → Team | Two people may share a name: the email is who someone is (SAME-NAMES). |
| Team | `id` | nothing beyond the key | `leadId` → Person |  |
| Cycle | `id` | `startDate` within the workspace, among goal years not removed | nothing |  |
| Goal | `id` | `cycleId` + `key` within the workspace, and a key is never given twice in a workspace, even after its goal is removed | `cycleId` → Cycle, `ownerId` → Person, `teamId` → Team, `parentId` → Goal (the one it feeds) | Two goals may share a title. The goals that feed one another never loop. |
| CheckIn | `id` | nothing beyond the key | `goalId` → Goal, `authorId` → Person | Not unique by goal and week: an owner may check in as often as they like, and the latest (by `postedAt`) is the week’s (ONE-PER-WEEK). A rebuild must not add that uniqueness. |
| Decision | `id` | nothing beyond the key | `goalId` → Goal, `checkInId` → CheckIn, `reviewId` → Review, `byId` → Person, `assigneeId` → Person |  |
| Ask | `id` | nothing beyond the key | `goalIds` → Goal (one or more), `askedBy` → Person, `recipientId` → Person, `reviewId` → Review, `checkInId` → CheckIn |  |
| Review | `id` | nothing beyond the key | `createdBy` → Person |  |
| Watch | `id` | `personId` + `kind` + `ref` within the workspace | `personId` → Person, `ref` → Goal, Goal (a tree) or a level, by `kind` |  |
| Comment | `id` | nothing beyond the key | `goalId` → Goal, `authorId` → Person | Faro stores a comment as a change-log entry; a rebuild gives comments a table of their own ([don’t copy this](../rebuild/dont-copy.md)). |
| Change | `id` | nothing beyond the key | `actorId` → Person, `goalId` → Goal | Never changed once written ([R8](../requirements/internal/r8-audit.md)). |
| Retro | `id` | `goalId` + `cycleId` within the workspace | `goalId` → Goal, `cycleId` → Cycle, `byId` → Person |  |
| SavedView | `id` | nothing beyond the key | `personId` → Person |  |
| ApiToken | `id` | `tokenHash` within every workspace | `personId` → Person, `createdBy` → Person |  |

## The records the core rules read

A rebuild of the core rules needs these: a **Cycle**, **Goal** (one of three kinds), **CheckIn**, **Person**, **Team**, **Decision** (what was said in a review), **Ask** and **Review**. The **Snapshot** holds a workspace’s records together. The rest (change log, watches, views, tokens, feedback, retros) belong to features around the rules.

### Id

```ts
type Id = string
```

### Person

Everyone can see everything; what a person can change follows from the goals they own. Admins (whoever set the workspace up, and anyone they add) also manage people and settings.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |

| `id` | `Id` | yes |  |
| `name` | `string` | yes |  |

| `initials` | `string` | yes |  |

| `admin` | `boolean` | yes |  |
| `email` | `string \| null` | no | Their email, lower case: how a spreadsheet, the import and the AI assistant tell people apart (two people can share a name). Required when someone is added; people added before emails existed have none until an admin fills it in. |
| `leftAt` | `string \| null` | no | Marked as left (domain/removal): gone from pickers, counts, reviews and Home; history keeps their name, "Name (left)". |
| `leftBy` | `Id \| null` | no |  |
| `removedAt` | `string \| null` | no | Deleted outright (only someone with no history): kept, hidden everywhere, restorable for 30 days. |
| `removedBy` | `Id \| null` | no |  |

### Level

How important a goal is to the organisation, for reporting at major reviews. Separate from what it feeds. A goal's level: an id from its cycle's levels (domain/levels.ts). Faro's three are 'north-star', 'svp' and 'team'.

```ts
type Level = string
```

### LevelDef

A level a workspace has: its id (stored on goals), its name, and the hint the goal form shows (domain/levels.ts).

| `id` | `Level` | yes |  |
| `name` | `string` | yes |  |
| `hint` | `string` | yes |  |
| `removedAt` | `string \| null` | no | Removed: goals moved off it; its name is kept for History. |

### Decision

What someone said about a goal in a review: seen, or a note. A question or an action said in a review is an ask (Ask, kinds question and action); review.ts's saidIn shows them beside the notes as one record of the session. The ask and action kinds here belong to data from before one ask model (asks.ts's upgradeAsks converts them), and approve and decline to data from before approvals were dropped.

Stopped goals with their check-ins and notes, people who left, ended reviews. Deleted records are in neither; they're read from the whole snapshot (Recently removed). |
| `proposed` | `Goal[]` | no | Set when a snapshot is scoped (domain/cycle scopeToCycle): this cycle's proposed goals (domain/proposed). Kept out of `goals`, as stopped goals are, so no count, status, check-in, review or wrap-up ever judges one; the places that list them (Goals with its filter, Find, their own page, the sheet and the tools) read them from here. |
| `history` | `{ from: string; checkInCycles: string[] }` | no | Set only when the snapshot was loaded with a window (ports/store LoadWindow, AX5 part 2): what was left out. Check-ins of cycles that ended before `from`, and change-log entries before it other than the anchors (ports/window.ts), are not loaded; `checkInCycles` names every cycle with any check-in, in the whole workspace, so a rule asking whether a cycle has one needn't load them. Older entries come a page at a time from Store.history. |

### Archive

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `goals` | `Goal[]` | yes |  |
| `checkIns` | `CheckIn[]` | yes |  |
| `decisions` | `Decision[]` | yes |  |
| `people` | `Person[]` | yes |  |
| `reviews` | `Review[]` | yes |  |

### AskStatus

Where an ask stands: open until the person asked responds (answered; an action: done) or it's taken back.

```ts
type AskStatus = 'open' | 'answered' | 'done' | 'withdrawn'
```

### AskKind

What an ask is for: a decision or help the owner needs from someone (often raised in a check-in); an update (someone asks a goal's owner to check in); a question for the owner (in a review or on the goal page); or an action (something someone agreed to do, usually in a review, by a week).

```ts
type AskKind = 'decision' | 'update' | 'question' | 'action'
```

### Ask

One way to ask (consolidation 4, 5 Nov): every ask that puts an obligation on someone. Who asked, who must respond, by when (optional), the goals it's about, and where it stands: open until it's answered (an action: done) or withdrawn, each said explicitly. Comments carry no obligation and aren't asks. Stored in okr_requests (extended by migration 0023; the table's name predates the other kinds). A decision ask can apply to several goals: an owner links their goal to one already raised for another, and one answer applies to all of them. The first goal is the one it was raised on.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `Id` | yes |  |
| `kind` | `AskKind` | yes |  |
| `goalIds` | `Id[]` | yes |  |
| `askedBy` | `Id` | yes |  |
| `recipientId` | `Id \| null` | yes | Who must respond: the person asked, the goal's owner (an update or a question), or whoever does the action. Null: anyone. |
| `ask` | `string` | yes | What was asked, in their words. |
| `status` | `AskStatus` | yes |  |
| `dueWeek` | `number \| null` | yes | The week it's due by, if any. |
| `reviewId` | `Id \| null` | yes | The review it was raised in, and that session's week, if it was. |
| `week` | `number \| null` | yes |  |
| `checkInId` | `Id \| null` | yes | The check-in that raised it (a decision or help). |
| `createdAt` | `string` | yes |  |
| `updatedAt` | `string` | yes |  |
| `answer` | `string \| null` | yes | The answer; for an action, the note it was marked done with (may be empty). |
| `answeredBy` | `Id \| null` | yes |  |
| `answeredAt` | `string \| null` | yes |  |

### SavedView

A saved view of the goals: a name, and the search, filters, sort, grouping and layout as a query string (the same one a shared link carries). It's one person's; an admin can pin one for everyone. Deleting sets deletedAt.

|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `Id` | yes |  |
| `personId` | `Id` | yes |  |
| `name` | `string` | yes |  |
| `params` | `string` | yes |  |
| `pinned` | `boolean` | yes |  |
| `createdAt` | `string` | yes |  |
| `updatedAt` | `string` | yes |  |
| `deletedAt` | `string \| null` | yes |  |
| `deletedBy` | `Id \| null` | no | Who deleted it. |

### ApiToken

A personal token an AI assistant uses to act as one person in one workspace. Only its hash is kept.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `Id` | yes |  |
| `personId` | `Id` | yes |  |
| `name` | `string` | yes | What it's for, e.g. "Claude on my laptop". |
| `tokenHash` | `string` | no | The SHA-256 hash of the token. Kept by the database, which never hands it back: the app and the MCP server's context see tokens without it. The demo's browser store keeps it. |
| `createdBy` | `Id` | yes |  |
| `createdAt` | `string` | yes |  |
| `lastUsedAt` | `string \| null` | yes |  |
| `revokedAt` | `string \| null` | yes |  |
| `builder` | `boolean` | no | Made as a builder token, before Faro opened its inbox (migration 0031): it now works as an ordinary token, and is labelled apart (backlog 10a). Read from the database (okr_token_list, migration 0034); never saved by the app. |

## Where they are stored

One Postgres database (Supabase). Each table holds one kind of record for every workspace (a `workspace_id` column), created by the migration named. `src/adapters/supabase/goalsStore.ts` maps rows to the records above; `src/data/rows.ts` does the field-by-field conversion. Every table, column, constraint, index and function as the database holds them after every migration: [schema.sql](schema.sql); who may read and change each: [access today](../rebuild/access-today.md).
